ontology.title: Human Description Instrument Ontology
ontology.description: A versioned ontology for describing and comparing personality tests, typology systems, psychometric instruments, symbolic self-description systems, and adjacent person-labeling frameworks.

dimensions.description: Top-level family membership for an instrument.
Primary things the instrument claims or appears to measure.
How the instrument encodes a person.
What kind of time-object the instrument assumes it captures.
What the instrument implicitly treats a person as.
How the instrument gathers data.
How responses become outputs.
General evidence type or truth-claim basis.
More granular evidence annotations.
How much meaning depends on interpreter vs instrument.
Resolution of the output model.
How global vs context-sensitive the outputs are.
What kind of change the instrument assumes is possible.
Likely distortions or misuse risks.
Common contexts where the instrument is used.
What the instrument is actually useful for.
Intended or normed user population.
Quality or presence of normative calibration.
How likely users are to fuse output with identity.
What kind of actionability the instrument supports.
Degree to which the instrument embeds a thick worldview.
Social and symbolic role beyond measurement.
Estimated usefulness as an input layer for downstream synthesis protocols.
Typical overlap pattern with other instruments.
